dataset.name: Component Identifier Knowledge Base
dataset.description: Structured semantic knowledge for identifying, classifying, understanding, composing, and verifying commonly used website and mobile-first web UI components.
principles: Prefer semantic component meaning over implementation-specific naming.
Use canonical component names for identification.
Treat aliases as synonyms or commonly used alternative terms.
Do not treat framework-specific component names as canonical component names.
Identify a component from its purpose, structure, behavior, and context rather than appearance alone.
Prefer the most specific applicable component.
Use contextual relationships to resolve ambiguous components.
Preserve responsive and mobile-first behavior when identifying components.
Distinguish structural components from interactive components.
Distinguish navigation components from action components.
Distinguish content components from feedback components.
A component may contain or compose other components.
Component identification should remain independent of framework implementation.

field_definitions.canonical_name: Official canonical component name used for component identification.
field_definitions.category: Primary semantic category of the component.
field_definitions.definition: Concise semantic definition of the component.
field_definitions.aliases: Common alternative names that may refer to the same component.
field_definitions.semantic_terms: Words and concepts that strongly indicate the component.
field_definitions.properties: Common conceptual properties or configuration dimensions.
field_definitions.content_model: Typical required, optional, conditional, and forbidden content.
field_definitions.identification_signals: Signals an AI can use to recognize the component.
field_definitions.anti_patterns: Patterns that should generally be avoided.
field_definitions.alternatives: Semantically related components that may be used instead in specific contexts.
field_definitions.verification: Ways to verify that the component is correctly identified and implemented.

entities.definition: A UI mechanism that allows users to move between destinations, pages, sections, or application areas.
entities.purpose: Provides discoverable access to destinations.
responsive_behavior: May transform into a Menu or App Drawer on narrow screens.
Navigation items must remain usable with touch input.
Horizontal navigation may become vertically stacked.
accessibility: Use semantic navigation landmarks where appropriate.
Expose the current destination when applicable.
identification_signals: Contains multiple destinations.
Items primarily change location or route.
Often appears in shared site or application structure.
Usually contains links rather than arbitrary actions.
anti_patterns: using unexplained icons as the only navigation mechanism
tradeoffs: Persistent navigation improves discoverability but consumes space.
implementation_notes: Navigation is a semantic system; its visual presentation may vary.

entities.definition: A top-level structural region containing introductory, branding, navigation, or utility content for a page or site.
entities.purpose: Provides consistent top-level context and access to primary controls.
responsive_behavior: May reduce visible navigation on mobile.
May expose an App Drawer trigger on narrow screens.
Content should not overflow horizontally.
identification_signals: Usually located at the top of a page or application shell.
Often spans the main content width.
Frequently contains branding and navigation.
anti_patterns: placing unrelated page content in a global header
tradeoffs: Persistent headers provide access but consume vertical space.
implementation_notes: Header is structural and may contain interactive components.

entities.definition: A bottom-level structural region containing supplementary information, navigation, legal information, or secondary actions.
entities.purpose: Provides persistent end-of-page information and secondary navigation.
responsive_behavior: Columns commonly stack on mobile.
Footer links should remain touch-friendly.
identification_signals: Usually appears after primary page content.
Contains secondary or legal information.
Often spans the full content width.
anti_patterns: placing primary task controls only in the footer
tradeoffs: More footer information improves discoverability but increases page length.
implementation_notes: Footer is normally a page-level structural component.
verification: Footer remains readable and usable on all supported widths.

entities.definition: A navigation surface that exposes primary application destinations, commonly through a persistent, collapsible, or off-canvas panel.
entities.purpose: Provides access to major application areas while preserving screen space.

conditional: close control when displayed as an overlay

responsive_behavior: Should generally become an overlay or off-canvas surface on small screens.
Must not unnecessarily consume mobile content width.
Open and close controls must remain accessible.
accessibility: Keyboard focus must be managed when used as an overlay.
identification_signals: Contains primary application navigation.
Appears as a side or off-canvas surface.
Can open, close, collapse, or expand.
Controls movement between major application areas.
anti_patterns: using a permanent desktop-width panel on narrow mobile screens
tradeoffs: Persistent access versus available content width.
implementation_notes: App Drawer is the canonical component name for primary application side navigation in this dataset.

entities.definition: A prominent introductory section that communicates the primary message, value proposition, or purpose of a page.
entities.purpose: Creates immediate context and directs users toward a primary goal.
responsive_behavior: Split layouts commonly stack on mobile.
Hero media may resize or move below text.
Primary content must remain immediately understandable.
accessibility: Do not rely on background images for essential information.
identification_signals: Large introductory region.
Contains a prominent headline.
Usually appears near the beginning of a page.
Often includes a primary call to action.
anti_patterns: hiding the primary message inside decorative media
tradeoffs: Visual prominence versus content density.
implementation_notes: Hero is a semantic content pattern rather than a specific visual style.

entities.definition: A thematic grouping of related content within a page.
entities.purpose: Organizes page content into meaningful regions.
responsive_behavior: Spacing and layout should adapt to viewport width.
identification_signals: Groups content around one theme or purpose.
Usually forms a distinct region of a page.
May have a heading and consistent spacing.
anti_patterns: using sections solely as generic wrappers without semantic purpose
tradeoffs: More sections improve structure but can fragment content.
implementation_notes: Section describes meaning, not merely a visual box.
verification: Grouped content has a coherent purpose.

entities.definition: A layout wrapper that constrains, aligns, or organizes content within available space.
entities.purpose: Controls content width and horizontal alignment.
responsive_behavior: Width should adapt to viewport size.
Horizontal padding should preserve usable content space.
accessibility: Container should not interfere with semantic structure.
identification_signals: Constrains content width.
Provides consistent horizontal alignment.
Usually has max-width and horizontal padding.
anti_patterns: deeply nesting containers without layout purpose
tradeoffs: Narrower content improves readability but reduces information density.
implementation_notes: Container is primarily a layout concept.

entities.definition: A bounded content grouping representing a related item, entity, or piece of information.
entities.purpose: Groups related content into a visually and semantically recognizable unit.
responsive_behavior: Card grids may change column count.
Card content should remain readable at narrow widths.
accessibility: Interactive cards must have clear focus behavior.
Do not make large regions clickable without accessible semantics.
identification_signals: Bounded visual grouping.
Contains related content about one item or concept.
Often repeated in grids or lists.
anti_patterns: putting an entire page inside a card
tradeoffs: Cards improve scanning but can fragment information.
implementation_notes: Card is a composition pattern, not necessarily an interactive element.

entities.definition: An interactive control that performs an action or triggers an operation.
entities.purpose: Allows users to perform actions.
responsive_behavior: Touch targets must remain sufficiently large on mobile.
Labels may adapt but must remain understandable.
accessibility: Use semantic button behavior for actions.
Expose disabled and loading states appropriately.
identification_signals: Performs an action rather than primarily changing location.
Often uses imperative labels such as Save, Submit, Delete, Open.
anti_patterns: using a div as an interactive button
tradeoffs: Button prominence should match action importance.
implementation_notes: Use Button for actions and Link for navigation.

entities.definition: An interactive text or media reference that navigates to another destination.
entities.purpose: Provides navigation between resources or locations.
responsive_behavior: Text should wrap naturally without breaking layout.
Touch targets should remain usable.
accessibility: Destination should be understandable from link text or context.
identification_signals: Its primary purpose is navigation.
Has a destination rather than an action.
anti_patterns: using click handlers on non-link elements for standard navigation
tradeoffs: Links communicate navigation semantics; buttons communicate actions.
implementation_notes: The Button-versus-Link distinction is semantic and behavioral.

entities.definition: A structured group of controls used to collect, validate, and submit user input.
entities.purpose: Collects and processes structured user data.
responsive_behavior: Fields commonly stack vertically on mobile.
Controls should remain touch-friendly.
accessibility: Every control needs an accessible label.
Validation errors should be communicated clearly.
identification_signals: Contains input controls intended for data collection.
Has submission or processing behavior.
anti_patterns: collecting user input without semantic form structure
tradeoffs: More validation improves data quality but increases interaction complexity.
implementation_notes: Form is the parent interaction structure for data entry.

entities.definition: A form control used to accept a single value from the user.
entities.purpose: Collects a single piece of user input.
responsive_behavior: Width should adapt to available space.
Appropriate mobile input types should be used.
accessibility: Do not rely only on placeholder text.
identification_signals: Accepts one user-entered value.
Usually appears as a bordered or underlined field.
anti_patterns: unlabeled input
tradeoffs: Short inputs are efficient for compact values; long values need other controls.
implementation_notes: Input is a single-value form control.

entities.definition: A form control that allows the user to choose one or more values from a predefined set of options.
entities.purpose: Provides constrained option selection.
responsive_behavior: Options must remain usable on mobile.
Long option labels should not cause overflow.
accessibility: Maintain keyboard and assistive technology support.
identification_signals: Presents predefined choices.
User selects from a set rather than typing arbitrary content.
anti_patterns: using Select for a very large searchable dataset without appropriate support
tradeoffs: Compact but slower for large option sets.
implementation_notes: Select is primarily a form input; Dropdown Menu is primarily an action/navigation menu.

entities.definition: A form control that represents an independent boolean choice or multiple selectable choices.
entities.purpose: Allows independent selection of one or more options.
responsive_behavior: Touch target should be easy to activate on mobile.
identification_signals: Represents independent on/off or multi-select choices.
anti_patterns: using checkbox for mutually exclusive choices
tradeoffs: Supports multiple independent choices but can become visually dense in large groups.
implementation_notes: Use Radio Button when only one option can be selected.

entities.definition: A form control used to select exactly one option from a mutually exclusive group.
entities.purpose: Allows one choice from a set of alternatives.
responsive_behavior: Options commonly stack vertically on mobile.
identification_signals: Multiple circular controls with only one selectable option in a group.
anti_patterns: using radio buttons for independent boolean choices
tradeoffs: Fast comparison for small option sets but poor for many options.
implementation_notes: Radio Button represents mutually exclusive selection.
verification: Only one option can be selected.

entities.definition: A multi-line form control used to collect longer text input.
entities.purpose: Collects multi-line or long-form user text.
responsive_behavior: Width should adapt to available space.
Avoid horizontal overflow.
identification_signals: Allows multiple lines of text.
Typically taller than a standard Input.
anti_patterns: using textarea for a short single-line value
tradeoffs: Supports rich text input but requires more vertical space.
implementation_notes: Textarea is intended for multi-line plain text unless explicitly enhanced.

entities.definition: Text that identifies the purpose or expected value of a form control.
entities.purpose: Makes form controls understandable and accessible.
responsive_behavior: Labels should remain visible and understandable on mobile.
accessibility: Associate labels programmatically with controls where applicable.
Do not rely solely on placeholder text.
identification_signals: Text directly identifying a nearby form control.
anti_patterns: removing labels because the UI looks visually clean
tradeoffs: Visible labels improve comprehension but consume space.
implementation_notes: Label is semantic form metadata, not merely decorative text.

entities.definition: A modal or non-modal surface that presents focused content or interaction above the current page context.
entities.purpose: Focuses attention on a contained task or piece of information.
responsive_behavior: May become full-screen or near-full-screen on mobile.
accessibility: Provide an accessible close mechanism when dismissible.
identification_signals: Temporarily presents focused content above or alongside the current context.
anti_patterns: using a dialog for simple navigation
tradeoffs: Focus improves task completion but interrupts surrounding context.
implementation_notes: Dialog describes the semantic interaction surface; Modal describes modal behavior.

entities.definition: An overlay interaction that prevents normal interaction with the underlying page until the modal interaction is resolved or dismissed.
entities.purpose: Creates a focused blocking interaction.
responsive_behavior: Often expands toward full-screen on mobile.
accessibility: Provide accessible name and close behavior.
identification_signals: Underlying page is blocked.
Usually has a backdrop.
Interaction must be completed or dismissed before returning.
anti_patterns: using modal for every minor interaction
tradeoffs: Strong attention control versus interruption.
implementation_notes: Modal is a behavioral characteristic; Dialog is the semantic surface.
verification: Background cannot be interacted with while modal is active.

entities.definition: A contextual floating surface anchored to a triggering element.
entities.purpose: Provides contextual information or controls without leaving the current context.
responsive_behavior: May reposition or expand on mobile to remain usable.
accessibility: Trigger and popover relationship must be clear.
identification_signals: Floating surface positioned relative to a trigger.
Does not necessarily block the entire page.
anti_patterns: using popover for essential content that cannot be discovered otherwise
tradeoffs: Saves space but can reduce discoverability.
implementation_notes: Popover is generally interactive; Tooltip is primarily informational.

entities.definition: A short contextual text label that provides additional information about an interface element.
entities.purpose: Clarifies unfamiliar controls or terminology.
responsive_behavior: Must not depend exclusively on hover on touch devices.
accessibility: Keyboard users must be able to access necessary information.
Do not put essential information only in tooltips.
identification_signals: Short informational text associated with a control.
Usually appears temporarily near its trigger.
anti_patterns: using tooltip as the only label for a critical action
tradeoffs: Reduces visible clutter but hides information until interaction.
implementation_notes: Tooltip is primarily informational and should remain brief.
verification: Information is accessible without mouse hover alone.

entities.definition: A contextual menu that reveals a list of actions or destinations from a trigger.
entities.purpose: Provides compact access to related actions or navigation choices.
responsive_behavior: May expand to a larger touch-friendly surface on mobile.
identification_signals: Hidden list appears after activating a trigger.
Items represent actions or destinations.
anti_patterns: using a dropdown for a very small number of always-visible choices
tradeoffs: Saves space but hides choices.
implementation_notes: Dropdown Menu is an interactive menu; Select is a form control.

entities.definition: A set of controls that switches between related content panels within the same contextual area.
entities.purpose: Organizes related content without requiring separate navigation.
responsive_behavior: May become horizontally scrollable or vertically stacked on mobile.
accessibility: Use proper tab semantics when appropriate.
identification_signals: Multiple peer controls switch content within the same region.
Only one panel is typically active at a time.
anti_patterns: using tabs for unrelated destinations
tradeoffs: Efficient content switching but hidden content can be overlooked.
implementation_notes: Tabs are for related peer content, not primary site navigation.
verification: Correct panel displays for each tab.

entities.definition: A vertically organized set of expandable and collapsible content panels.
entities.purpose: Progressively reveals content while conserving vertical space.
responsive_behavior: Particularly suitable for narrow screens.
Panels should not cause horizontal overflow.
identification_signals: Repeated headings or triggers expand/collapse associated content vertically.
anti_patterns: hiding essential information that users must always see
tradeoffs: Saves vertical space but hides information.
implementation_notes: Accordion is a progressive disclosure pattern.
verification: Each panel expands and collapses predictably.

entities.definition: A structured presentation of related data arranged in rows and columns.
entities.purpose: Enables comparison and scanning of structured data.
responsive_behavior: May scroll horizontally when necessary.
May transform into stacked records on mobile when semantics permit.
accessibility: Avoid forcing complex tables into inaccessible layouts.
identification_signals: Data is explicitly organized into rows and columns.
Column relationships are meaningful.
anti_patterns: using tables purely for page layout
tradeoffs: Excellent for comparison but can be difficult on narrow screens.
implementation_notes: Table should be used for tabular relationships, not generic layout.

entities.definition: A collection of related items presented as an ordered, unordered, or structured sequence.
entities.purpose: Organizes repeated related content.
responsive_behavior: Items may stack vertically and adapt spacing on mobile.
identification_signals: Repeated peer items share a common structure.
anti_patterns: using unrelated content as one list
tradeoffs: Simple and scalable but can become visually repetitive.
implementation_notes: List is appropriate when items share semantic structure.
verification: Items have consistent semantics and order.

entities.definition: A navigation mechanism that divides a collection of content into discrete pages or result sets.
entities.purpose: Allows users to move through large datasets or content collections.
responsive_behavior: Controls may simplify on mobile.
Touch targets must remain usable.
identification_signals: Controls represent discrete pages of a larger collection.
anti_patterns: pagination for very small datasets
tradeoffs: Improves performance and scanning but introduces navigation steps.
implementation_notes: Pagination is appropriate for discrete result sets.
verification: Current, next, and previous states work correctly.

entities.definition: A hierarchical navigation trail showing the user's location within a site or application structure.
entities.purpose: Provides contextual location and upward navigation.
responsive_behavior: May collapse intermediate levels on mobile.
Must avoid horizontal overflow.
identification_signals: Displays hierarchical path such as Home > Category > Current Page.
anti_patterns: using breadcrumbs where no hierarchy exists
tradeoffs: Provides context but adds little value for shallow structures.
implementation_notes: Breadcrumb represents hierarchy, not merely browser history.

entities.definition: A compact visual label used to communicate status, category, count, or metadata.
entities.purpose: Provides concise contextual information.
responsive_behavior: Should remain compact without becoming unreadable.
accessibility: Status information must not rely only on color.
identification_signals: Small compact label attached to another content item.
anti_patterns: using badges for primary actions
tradeoffs: Compact but limited space for explanation.
implementation_notes: Badge is informational, not primarily interactive.
verification: Meaning remains clear without color alone.

entities.definition: A visible message that communicates important information, status, warning, or error to the user.
entities.purpose: Communicates information that requires user awareness.
responsive_behavior: Messages should wrap naturally on mobile.
accessibility: Use appropriate live-region behavior when needed.
Do not rely solely on color.
identification_signals: Prominent message communicates system or contextual status.
anti_patterns: using alerts for ordinary page content
tradeoffs: Persistent visibility improves awareness but consumes space.
implementation_notes: Alert is generally persistent or inline compared with Toast.

entities.definition: A temporary notification that appears independently of the main document flow.
entities.purpose: Provides brief feedback about an action or event.
responsive_behavior: Must remain visible without covering critical mobile controls.
accessibility: Do not make critical information disappear too quickly.
identification_signals: Temporary message appears outside normal document flow.
Usually disappears automatically or after dismissal.
anti_patterns: using toast for critical information that must persist
tradeoffs: Low interruption but easy to miss.
implementation_notes: Toast is transient; Alert is generally persistent.

entities.definition: A visual indicator communicating the completion level of a task or process.
entities.purpose: Shows measurable progress toward completion.
responsive_behavior: Should scale with available width.
identification_signals: Shows a measurable amount of completion.
anti_patterns: using progress when no measurable progress exists
tradeoffs: Determinate progress reassures users; inaccurate progress is misleading.
implementation_notes: Use Progress for measurable task completion.
verification: Displayed progress corresponds to actual process state.

entities.definition: An animated indicator used to communicate an ongoing indeterminate operation or loading state.
entities.purpose: Shows that a process is currently active.
responsive_behavior: Must remain visible at appropriate size on small screens.
accessibility: Provide an accessible loading status when needed.
identification_signals: Animated circular or similar indicator without measurable completion.
anti_patterns: using spinner when actual progress can be communicated
tradeoffs: Simple but provides little information about completion time.
implementation_notes: Spinner communicates activity, not percentage completion.

entities.definition: A placeholder representation of content shown while the actual content is loading.
entities.purpose: Preserves layout context and reduces perceived loading disruption.
responsive_behavior: Skeleton dimensions should correspond to the responsive content layout.
accessibility: Loading state should be communicated appropriately.
identification_signals: Placeholder shapes mimic expected content structure.
anti_patterns: using skeleton when content appears instantly
tradeoffs: Maintains layout but requires matching placeholder design.
implementation_notes: Skeleton is useful when content structure is known before data arrives.
verification: Loaded content matches placeholder structure closely.

entities.definition: A compact visual representation of a person, account, or entity.
entities.purpose: Provides recognizable identity context.
responsive_behavior: Size may reduce on mobile while remaining recognizable.
accessibility: Provide appropriate alternative text or accessible name when meaningful.
identification_signals: Small circular or bounded representation of a person/entity.
anti_patterns: using avatar as the only indicator of identity when text is required
tradeoffs: Compact identity representation versus limited detail.
implementation_notes: Avatar is identity-oriented; Image is generic media.
verification: Identity remains understandable when image fails.

entities.definition: A visual media element used to communicate, illustrate, or decorate content.
entities.purpose: Presents visual information or supporting imagery.
responsive_behavior: Images should scale without distortion or overflow.
Use responsive image strategies where appropriate.
accessibility: Provide appropriate alternative text for meaningful images.
Decorative images should not create unnecessary accessibility noise.
identification_signals: Displays raster or vector visual media.
anti_patterns: embedding essential text only inside images
tradeoffs: Visual communication versus bandwidth and accessibility requirements.
implementation_notes: Image is media; Icon is typically symbolic UI graphics.

entities.definition: A compact symbolic graphic representing an action, concept, status, or object.
entities.purpose: Provides compact visual recognition and supports interface meaning.
responsive_behavior: Maintain usable size and visual clarity on small screens.
accessibility: Decorative icons should not add unnecessary accessible content.
identification_signals: Small symbolic graphic with compact semantic meaning.
anti_patterns: using icons as unexplained replacement for all text
tradeoffs: Compact but can be ambiguous without labels.
implementation_notes: Icon is a symbolic UI element rather than general imagery.

entities.definition: A media component used to present moving visual and audio content.
entities.purpose: Communicates information or experiences through time-based media.
responsive_behavior: Maintain aspect ratio.
Controls must remain usable on mobile.
identification_signals: Time-based visual media with playback controls or automatic playback.
anti_patterns: autoplaying audio without user intent
tradeoffs: Rich communication versus bandwidth and interaction cost.
implementation_notes: Video should adapt to viewport width and connection conditions.

entities.definition: A rotating or horizontally navigable presentation of multiple related items within a shared viewport.
entities.purpose: Presents multiple items while conserving space.
responsive_behavior: May display fewer items on mobile.
Swipe interaction may be supported.
Controls must remain accessible.
accessibility: Users must be able to pause automatic movement.
Slides should be navigable without pointer gestures alone.
identification_signals: Multiple items share one viewport.
Previous/next or swipe interaction changes visible item.
anti_patterns: hiding critical content exclusively inside a carousel
tradeoffs: Saves space but reduces simultaneous visibility.
implementation_notes: Carousels should not hide essential information from users who cannot interact with them.
verification: Controls and swipe behavior work where supported.

entities.definition: A component that allows users to locate content, resources, or records by entering or selecting search criteria.
entities.purpose: Provides direct access to information across a potentially large collection.
responsive_behavior: May expand or become a dedicated screen on mobile.
Input and controls must remain touch-friendly.
accessibility: Clearly communicate loading and result states.
identification_signals: Accepts a query intended to locate matching content or records.
anti_patterns: search for collections small enough to browse directly
tradeoffs: Efficient for large collections but requires good result relevance.
implementation_notes: Search is a task-oriented discovery component.
verification: Results and no-results states are clear.

entities.definition: A structured collection of commands, actions, or destinations presented as selectable items.
entities.purpose: Groups related choices into a compact interaction surface.
responsive_behavior: May become full-width or stacked on mobile.
accessibility: Use appropriate menu semantics when applicable.
identification_signals: Contains a collection of peer selectable commands or destinations.
anti_patterns: using menu semantics for arbitrary static lists
tradeoffs: Compact choice presentation versus hidden options.
implementation_notes: Menu is the collection; Dropdown Menu describes a menu revealed from a trigger.
verification: All items are reachable and understandable.

entities.definition: A panel that slides or appears from an edge of the viewport to present content or controls.
entities.purpose: Provides additional content or controls without permanently occupying page space.
responsive_behavior: Especially useful for mobile interfaces.
May occupy more viewport width on small screens.
accessibility: Provide accessible name and close control.
identification_signals: Panel enters from a viewport edge.
Usually hidden until triggered.
anti_patterns: using Drawer when persistent navigation is semantically more appropriate
tradeoffs: Preserves page space but temporarily hides content behind an overlay.
implementation_notes: Drawer is generic; App Drawer specifically represents primary application navigation.
verification: Opening, closing, focus, and mobile behavior work.

entities.definition: A visual representation of dates organized into calendar periods such as months, weeks, or days.
entities.purpose: Allows users to understand, browse, or interact with dates.
responsive_behavior: Calendar may switch to a more compact or list-oriented mobile presentation.
accessibility: Dates must be keyboard navigable where interactive.
Selected and current dates must be distinguishable.
identification_signals: Displays dates in a grid or chronological calendar structure.
anti_patterns: using a full calendar for a simple single-date choice
tradeoffs: Excellent for date context but can be excessive for simple selection.
implementation_notes: Calendar represents date visualization; Date Picker represents date selection interaction.
verification: Navigation and selection work where interactive.

entities.definition: A form control that allows users to select a date or date range.
entities.purpose: Provides structured date selection.
responsive_behavior: Calendar surface should adapt to mobile viewport.
Touch targets must remain usable.
accessibility: Selected date must be announced appropriately.
Input must have an accessible label.
identification_signals: User is explicitly selecting a date as form data.
Often opens a Calendar interface.
anti_patterns: ambiguous date formats
tradeoffs: Visual selection reduces date-format errors but adds interaction complexity.
implementation_notes: Date Picker is an input component; Calendar is the date visualization mechanism it may use.

identification_rules.rule: Use Button when the primary purpose is performing an action. Use Link when the primary purpose is navigating to another destination.
Use App Drawer when primary application navigation is presented through a side, collapsible, or off-canvas navigation surface. Use Navigation for the navigation system itself.
Use App Drawer for primary application navigation. Use Drawer for a generic edge-originating panel containing arbitrary content or controls.
Dialog identifies the focused interaction surface. Modal identifies the blocking behavior that prevents interaction with the underlying page.
Use Popover for interactive contextual content. Use Tooltip for short supplementary information.
Use Select for choosing form values. Use Dropdown Menu for actions or navigation choices.
Use Navigation for a destination-oriented navigation system. Use Menu for a structured collection of commands or choices.
Use Tabs to switch between related content within the same context. Use Navigation to move between destinations.
Use Tabs when users switch between peer content panels. Use Accordion when users expand or collapse vertically organized content.
Use Alert for persistent or important visible messages. Use Toast for temporary feedback.
Use Progress when completion can be measured. Use Spinner when activity is indeterminate.
Use Spinner to indicate activity. Use Skeleton when the expected content structure is known and being loaded.
Use Calendar for date visualization or browsing. Use Date Picker when the user is selecting a date as input.
Use Image for general visual media. Use Icon for compact symbolic UI meaning.
Use Checkbox for independent selections. Use Radio Button when exactly one option must be selected from a group.

responsive_principles: All components must remain usable on narrow mobile viewports.
Avoid horizontal overflow unless horizontal scrolling is intentional.
Navigation should transform rather than simply shrink when necessary.
Multi-column layouts should collapse or adapt appropriately.
Overlays must remain within the usable viewport.
Text must remain readable without requiring excessive zoom.
Component states must remain understandable on touch devices.
Hover-only interactions must have an appropriate touch or keyboard equivalent.
Critical content must not depend exclusively on hover, animation, or hidden interaction.
accessibility_principles: Use semantic HTML concepts where applicable.
Every interactive control must have an accessible name.
Keyboard interaction must be supported for interactive components.
Do not communicate meaning using color alone.
Dialogs, modals, drawers, and popovers require appropriate focus management.
Dynamic feedback must be communicated appropriately.
Media should provide appropriate alternatives such as captions or text alternatives.
Component identification should consider semantic purpose rather than visual styling alone.

identity_checks: Component purpose matches the observed behavior.
Component is not incorrectly identified from appearance alone.
Aliases do not override the canonical component name.
structure_checks: Nested components have a logical parent-child relationship.
Component composition does not create unnecessary duplication.
responsive_checks: Component works at larger viewport widths.
accessibility_checks: Accessible names are present where required.
behavior_checks: Loading, empty, error, and success states are represented where applicable.

normalization.canonical_name_rule: Always use the canonical_name value when assigning an identified component.
normalization.alias_rule: Aliases may be used to recognize user or source terminology but must resolve to the canonical component.
normalization.case_rule: Canonical component names use title case.
normalization.implementation_rule: Framework-specific implementations must not replace canonical semantic component names.
normalization.mobile_first_rule: Responsive identification must prioritize the component's semantic purpose even when its visual presentation changes across breakpoints.
